page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Substitute t = logx
steps.why: 1/(x logx) dx splits naturally into (1/logx)·(dx/x), and the second factor is exactly dt once t=logx — leaving the most basic ∫dt/t form.
common_mistakes: Trying to integrate 1/(x logx) as a product using integration by parts instead of the direct substitution.
Missing that dx/x, not dx alone, is what converts to dt.
steps.memory_tip: ∫dt/t = log|t| is the single most basic log-form integral in the whole chapter — recognise it immediately.

steps.label: Integrate and back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: ∫dt/t = log|t| + c, and substituting t=logx back in gives the final answer in x, with the modulus bars kept since logx can be negative for 0<x<1.
common_mistakes: Dropping the modulus bars, which makes the antiderivative undefined for 0<x<1 where logx<0.
Forgetting to substitute logx back in for t.
steps.memory_tip: Keep |·| on the final log — logx is negative for x between 0 and 1, so the bars are not optional here.
